content:
Let \(k\) be written in base \(503\):
\[
k=503q+s,\qquad 0\le s<503.
\]
Since
\[
10000=19\cdot 503+443,
\]
Lucas’s theorem gives
\[
\binom{10000}{k}\equiv \binom{19}{q}\binom{443}{s}\pmod{503}.
\]

Also,
\[
503\equiv 1 \pmod{502},
\]
so
\[
k=503q+s\equiv q+s \pmod{502}.
\]

The binomial coefficient \(\binom{443}{s}\) is nonzero modulo \(503\) only for \(0\le s\le 443\), and \(0\le q\le 19\). Therefore every nonzero term modulo \(503\) has
\[
q+s\le 19+443=462.
\]

Thus for \(r>462\), there are no nonzero contributions modulo \(503\), so
\[
S_r\equiv 0\pmod{503}.
\]

For \(0\le r\le 462\), the coefficient contributions give
\[
S_r\equiv \sum_{q+s=r}\binom{19}{q}\binom{443}{s}
=\binom{462}{r}\pmod{503}.
\]
Since \(462<503\), \(\binom{462}{r}\) is not divisible by \(503\). Hence \(S_r\not\equiv 0\pmod{503}\) for \(0\le r\le 462\).

So the multiples of \(503\) among \(S_0,S_1,\dots,S_{501}\) are exactly those with
\[
463\le r\le 501.
\]
That gives
\[
501-463+1=39.
\]

\[
\boxed{39}
\]
